How it went and what you learned

tell work you're too ill to come

model: I'd like to talk about the time I came down with the flu right before a job interview, which was about three years ago. It was for a position at an international company that I'd really wanted to work for, and I'd been preparing for weeks. Two days before the interview, I started feeling under the weather, and by the next evening I had a fever and a splitting headache. My mum said I should just call the company and ask to reschedule, but I was worried they'd think I wasn't serious. So I decided to push through. The doctor at the clinic told me I had to rest up and drink plenty of fluids, and she said I'd better take some paracetamol an hour before the interview. So that's exactly what I did. On the day, I still felt awful, and my voice sounded quite rough. Luckily, it was an online interview, so at least I didn't have to travel. I was supposed to talk about my experience for five minutes, but I kept losing my train of thought. In the end, I was honest and told them I wasn't feeling well, and they were surprisingly kind about it. I didn't get that job, but they invited me to apply again six months later, and that time I got it. Looking back, I think I ought to have asked to reschedule. I was back on my feet a week later, and I'd probably have performed much better.
